llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only policy for safe failure handling; its requirements and instructions align with its stated purpose and it does not request credentials, installs, or system access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the instructions: the SKILL.md is a failure-handling protocol (bounded retries, escalation, redact raw traces). It does not ask for unrelated capabilities, binaries, or credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions stay within the failure-handling domain (no file reads, no env access, no external endpoints specified). Two practical assumptions may require platform capabilities: (1) the agent must be able to verify outcomes (send messages, create events, write files) to mark tasks done, and (2) obeying cooldowns/waiting for next allowed slot implies scheduling or rate-limit awareness. These are reasonable but rely on the agent/runtime to provide the checks and wait behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only reduces surface area; nothing will be downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The SKILL.md does not reference hidden secrets or request unrelated tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal invocation model. The skill does not request permanent presence, system-wide changes, or modifications to other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This is a low-risk, instruction-only policy that tells an agent how to behave when tools fail — it doesn't install code or ask for secrets. Before installing, confirm that your agent/runtime can actually perform the verifications the protocol expects (e.g., check that messages/events/files can be verified and that waiting for rate-limit windows is supported). Also ensure your organization is comfortable with the escalation wording and that any redaction of stack traces or internal payloads follows your privacy/compliance rules. Test the protocol in a non-production environment to confirm it behaves as intended.
